data.narrative:
Natilus is a Series A drone and autonomous systems company that has raised $16M to date. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector comprises eight private peers—including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air—with no public comparables available. A narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints within the sector; only one adjacent-stage comparable existed, falling short of the three-company minimum threshold for statistical reliability.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to later-stage advancement. Using the $16M total raised as a proxy baseline, this method implies a valuation of $32M. The stage-progression approach is grounded in observed venture capital step-up patterns between funding rounds, though its applicability depends on Natilus achieving trajectory consistent with peer advancement rates.

The triangulated range derived from available applicable methods is $27M (low) to $37M (high), centered on a $32M median. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single methodological input rather than true triangulation. Key uncertainties include the company's product-market fit trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peer cohorts, and whether near-term milestones will support or challenge the implied step-up multiple. A peer-median valuation becomes viable only upon identification of additional same-stage comparables with disclosed valuations.
